verdicts.reason: The conflation is still live: rules.js:77 sets `known.koreanEdu = person.eduKorea ? person.edu : 0`. In a node run, UZ age 35 on E-7-1 with doctorate, the Korea box ticked, STEM and top-100 gets F-5-15 open with '✓ matches'. Unticked, the same reader gets BLOCKED [koreanEdu]. So a Korean bachelor's plus a foreign PhD is credited with a Korean doctorate, while F-5-15 is the domestic-doctorate route. The mirror case also reproduces: a D-10-1 master's holder with both boxes unticked has F-2-7S BLOCKED [koreanEdu, stem], while a reader who leaves education blank sees it open. The proposed fix needs changing. Making `stem` undefined whenever its box is unticked would leave readers no way to say 'not STEM'. It also drops eduKorea, which old shared links and the tests still use (rules.test.mjs and scenarios.test.mjs pass eduKorea). Use a separate tri-state question for each fact instead. The new labels need all four languages. I could not fetch law.go.kr from this session (search budget used up, DNS failure), so the F-5-15 meaning rests on the 2026 KIS manual heading and the 비자 내비게이터 (KIS Visa Navigator guide) quote kept in the audit.

verdicts.reason: The original claim, that only one group's reasons are shown, was right, and the proposed union has since landed (rules.js:174-176). The union over-reports, though. In a node run, a 35-year-old Uzbek with high school and 0 years who looks at E-7-1 from NONE now gets reasons [edu, experience, koreanEdu, ageUnder, countries]. On screen that reads 'Education doesn't match', 'Needs more work experience', 'Age doesn't match' and 'Not for your nationality'. The last two come only from the narrow asiaPilot alternative (UZ is not in it). E-7-1 itself has no age or nationality bar, so those two tags mislead in a new way. Leave out alternatives that fail on facts the reader can never change, unless every alternative fails that way. A simulated version gives [edu, experience, koreanEdu] for both UZ and VN, still blocks F-2-R on notAfter and F-6-1 on spouse, and passes all 18 tests in tests/rules.test.mjs.

verdicts.reason: The code reading is right: for non-level facts, `gives` only fills a gap (rules.js:118). That is the correct behaviour, and the proposed ESTABLISHES override is harmful. The suggested data half (`gives: {spouse: korean}` on F-6-1) has already landed (commit 068176a) and causes a live misrecommendation. In a node run, a reader who left spouse blank now sees F-6-1 -> F-6-3 and F-6-1 -> F-6-2 BLOCKED [spouse]; with that gives line removed, both are open. Simulating the override as well makes F-6-3 and F-6-2 blocked for every reader, including one who answered exKorean. It also opens F-5-2 for an F-6-1 holder who is already divorced. engine.md says a `gives` must hold after COMPLETING the visa. F-6-1 is exactly the status people leave when the marriage ends: F-6-2's own text says 'After the marriage to a Korean citizen ended ... While still married, you stay on F-6-1', and F-6-2/F-6-3 have `change` document lists. The fix is to remove the gives line, not to override answers. The F-5-2 move already carries `needs: {spouse: korean}`, and a blank spouse never blocks it.

Add a test to tests/scenarios.test.mjs: for uz() with spouse unanswered, on path ['NONE','F-6-1'], F-6-3 is not blocked and F-6-2 (with koreanChild: true) is not blocked; with spouse 'exKorean' on path ['F-6-1'], F-5-2 is blocked.
